description: Probe for #1400 stage A. An inline copy of templates/minimax/generated-subject-reference that changes only the draw step's prompt and size ('subject_prompt', 'draw_width', 'draw_height'), and adds a last step scoring the clip's faces against the draw (analyze_face_drift; the largest face, so the head panel on a sheet). Arm P draws one 768x768 portrait; arm S a 1344x768 face-once sheet, with its own subject_definitions in 'prompt'. The H3 step is the template's at its defaults (960x544, 124 frames, turbo, 9 steps).
summary: #1400 A: one arm of the face-once sheet probe - draw, H3 clip, face score.

vram_estimate.reason: Ref2VA holds every reference's encoding resident beside the video latents, so the ceiling is a fixed base, a per-voxel term for the VAE decode's conv3d activation (width * height * num_frames), and a per-reference term. Classified against the 24 GB entry from the #479 field report (lem, RTX 3090 24 GB, int4 + 768p turbo LoRA, 9 steps, 2026-09-25/26) at 1344x768: 175 frames x 2 refs, 209 x 2 and 175 x 3 ran (projected 22.83, 23.77 and 23.83 GB); 209 x 3 OOM'd in reference encode needing a further 5.1 GB and 260 x 1 OOM'd at denoise step 1 needing a further 4.8 GB (projected 24.77 and 24.18 GB). The refused allocations are lower bounds, not peaks, so this is a classification with about 0.2 GB of margin either side, not a fitted curve. bytes_per_voxel is unchanged from #324's calibration (job 282172105da1); base_gb drops 0.3 GB now the references are counted separately

variables.prompt:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the fisherman in <Picture 1>, a man in his sixties with close-cropped grey hair and a short grey beard, in a navy cable-knit wool jumper under an open yellow oilskin jacket, whose face, hair, clothes and proportions define his appearance for the whole video.

summary:
[reference generation] The target video shows <Subject 1> speaking directly to camera in a dim wooden net loft by a harbour, in one continuous take.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the face, hair, clothes and proportions from <Picture 1> are kept exactly, with the head, jaw and shoulders newly animated to speak.

detailed_description:
The target video is in realistic photographic style. [Shot 1] A medium close-up frames <Subject 1> from the chest up, centred and facing camera in a dim wooden net loft by a harbour, coiled nets and floats hanging on the plank wall behind him, held as one continuous shot. A grey window light falls from the left across his face and beard, the background staying dark and well behind in shallow focus. <Subject 1> (S1), a low and weathered male voice, unhurried and dry, says <d>[English] The tide never asks permission. You learn to be ready when it turns.</d> The jaw and lips move in natural synchronisation with the speech and settle closed at the end of the line. Between phrases <Subject 1> shifts weight very slightly and the head drifts a few degrees off centre and back, with the eyes staying on the lens and blinking at a natural rate. The camera holds a static shot throughout.

overall_soundscape:
A quiet, close room tone at an even level from the first frame to the last, with faint water lapping below the boards and a single soft creak of the oilskin as <Subject 1> shifts weight.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A

num_frames.reason: the video VAE encodes 17 * n + 5 frames, and MiniMax-H3 generates between 5 and 15 seconds at 24 fps

width.reason: MiniMax-H3's pipeline refuses a `width` or `height` that is not a multiple of 32, and only after the weights have loaded; refused here instead, with no 'snap', since rounding would be a silent change to the size asked for
